title: AskGrokWallet receipt, signature version 3
description: A receipt is an approval row plus an Ed25519 signature over 22 of its fields. This schema describes the shape; it cannot describe the signature, so passing validation says nothing about authenticity. To check that, run https://askgrokwallet.io/verify-receipt.mjs — a single dependency-free file that re-implements the check from the spec rather than importing the issuer's code. Two rules matter more than any type here: (1) the 22 signed fields are canonicalized in the FIXED order given by x-signedFields, not alphabetically, and a missing, undefined or null value is written as null rather than omitted, so absent and null are indistinguishable to the signature; (2) nested objects are canonicalized with their keys SORTED, so two key orders of the same execute intent cannot yield two valid signatures. canonical = "v3:" + JSON.stringify(that object).

x-unsignedFields.sigVersion: output. Deliberately NOT read when verifying: the version is fixed at 3 by the verifier, because a receipt that picks its own canonicalization could pick an easier one
x-unsignedFields.signedAt: output. Participates in the hash-chain entry preimage as a string, but is not inside the signature
x-unsignedFields.settlementClaimedAt: deliberately unsigned. The sweeper sets it to claim a row before executing, so it changes AFTER the receipt is signed; putting it in the signature would force a re-sign and a new chain entry for an event that moved no money
x-unsignedFields.riskLevel: there is no such field. Risk pre-check output rides inside the signed `reason` text on purpose — a 23rd signed field would make this sigVersion 4 and invalidate every receipt already issued

id.description: Also the requestId the controller consumes on-chain, which is why the same receipt cannot pay twice.

summary.description: Free text from the caller. Length-prefixed in the chain preimage precisely because it is attacker-controlled.

amountUsd.description: Use an integer or at most two decimals. JSON.stringify writes 80, never 80.0, and a value large or small enough to be written in exponential form will not round-trip across implementations.

target.description: A merchant label, NOT a payee address. The address is execute.to.

mode.description: Which trust boundary was in force. advisory and watchdog cannot stop a direct chain signature; only guarded reverts on-chain.

intentKind.description: Present for consequential non-payment actions (cancel, downgrade, delete).

verdict.description: What the policy engine decided before any human saw it.

reason.description: Human-readable justification. Risk pre-check output appears here — see x-unsignedFields.riskLevel.

status.description: Read auto-allowed carefully: the policy allowed it and NO human was asked. Only `pending` ever waited for a person. `executed` and `execution_failed` are set by the sweeper after the chain answers.

decision.description: `auto` means the policy engine decided; there was no human decision to record.

execute.description: The payment intent. Exactly these four keys are kept; anything else the caller sends is dropped BEFORE signing, so the intent means one thing. If all four are absent the whole object is null.

rail.description: evm:<chainId> when derived from execute. A web2 rail such as stripe:subscription only WITNESSES a charge and cannot block one — do not read it as enforcement.

railRef.description: The rail's own identifier for a non-EVM payment.

txHash.description: Set when the sweeper executes. Signed since v3: under v2 it was outside the signature, so a receipt still verified after its destination and hash were swapped.

signature.description: Ed25519 over the UTF-8 bytes of the canonical string.

sigVersion.description: Only 3 verifies. v1 read its version off the untrusted row and had a hardcoded fallback secret; v2 signed 13 fields and left the destination out. Older rows read as unverified, which is the honest answer.
